```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", echo = FALSE)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
# The results are precomputed (see "How the results were made" at the end) and read from small CSV
# files next to this vignette, so the vignette builds without running any comparison.
tab <- function(name) utils::read.csv(file.path("packageComparison", paste0(name, ".csv")), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
has <- function(name) file.exists(file.path("packageComparison", paste0(name, ".csv")))
show <- function(x, ...) knitr::kable(x, row.names = FALSE, ...)
whatif <- tab("whatifSummary")
gformula <- tab("gformulaSummary")
```

This vignette compares CloneCensorWeight with independent implementations of the same quantities:
the book code of *Causal Inference: What If*, the `ccwr` package, and the truth of the package's own
simulator. Each comparison states in advance what it requires. A *gated* comparison has a pass/fail
criterion. A *reported* comparison is shown without one, because the two implementations make
different, documented choices, so exact agreement is not expected.

The component-level references (`survival`, `sandwich`, `boot`, `glmnet`) are tested on every check,
and the cross-checks against `ccwr`, `ipw`, `TTE`, `trtswitch`, `geepack` and `simcausal`
(`tests/testthat/test-crossChecks-*.R`) run when `CCW_RUN_CROSSCHECKS=true`, from the developers'
cross-check runner. This vignette shows the end-to-end comparisons. Comparisons whose reference package or data were not available are listed as skipped,
with the reason.

## Overview

```{r overview}
show(tab("overview"), col.names = c("Comparison", "Criterion", "Result"))
```

The packages the comparisons use, and whether they were installed when the results were made:

```{r packages}
show(tab("packages"), col.names = c("Tier", "Package", "Version", "Status"))
```

## What If: the G = 0 reduction

With a grace period of zero days, `initiateWithin(0)` versus `notInitiateWithin(0)` is a point
treatment at time zero: each person follows exactly one strategy from the start, and both censoring
models reduce to one logistic model for the treatment on day 0, the propensity score. The
clone-censor-weight analysis must then reproduce an ordinary inverse-probability-weighted survival
analysis. Program 17.3 of Hernán and Robins's *Causal Inference: What If* is such an analysis: the
effect of quitting smoking on death over 120 months in the NHEFS data, with stabilized weights from a
logistic propensity model and a weighted pooled logistic hazards model with a quadratic in time and
its interaction with treatment.

The CloneCensorWeight analysis uses the 17.3 covariates as fixed covariates with no prior, stabilized
weights without truncation, and a pooled logistic outcome model with a raw quadratic time basis and
arm-by-time interaction. Months are coded as days with the risk window starting on day 1, so the
day-0 treatment precedes the first interval. The gate is 1e-6 on the outcome-model coefficients and
on the risks at every month, against a fresh run of the book code. The book models `event == 0`, so
its coefficients have the opposite sign.

```{r whatifSummary}
x <- whatif
for (column in 2:4) x[[column]] <- formatC(x[[column]], format = "e", digits = 1)
show(x, col.names = c("Reference", "Largest coefficient difference",
                                       "Largest risk difference", "Largest relative weight difference", "Gate"))
```

```{r whatifCoefficients}
x <- tab("whatifCoefficients")
x$difference <- formatC(x$difference, format = "e", digits = 1)
show(x, digits = 10, col.names = c("Term", "Book (event == 0)", "CloneCensorWeight", "Sum"))
```

```{r whatifRisks}
x <- tab("whatifRisks")
show(x, digits = 6, col.names = c("Month", "Book, quit", "CCW, quit", "Book, did not quit", "CCW, did not quit"))
```

The book shows the 120-month curves only in a plot; the table gives their values. The NHEFS data are
not distributed with this package. The test `test-crossChecks-whatif.R` repeats this comparison when
the environment variable `CCW_NHEFS_PATH` names a local copy of `nhefs.csv`, from the book's web page,
and skips otherwise.

## G-methods on simulated data

The parametric g-formula (`gfoRmula`, `gfoRmulaICE`) and TMLE (`lmtp`) estimate the same risks as a
clone-censor-weight analysis under a different set of modelling assumptions. The plan compares them on
data from `simulateCloneCensorWeightData()`, whose true risks `computeTrueRisks()` computes by
simulating each regime directly: data-generating process (a), in which treatment acts only after the
grace period; a grace period of 7 days, a daily horizon of 56 days, one binary confounder and `r format(gformula$n, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)`
persons per replicate.

**The g-formula packages were not installed** (`r gformula$missingGformulaPackages`), so only the
CloneCensorWeight half of this comparison ran: `r format(gformula$replicates, big.mark = ",")` replicates
(`r gformula$failedReplicates` failed), censoring models with the package defaults but no prior
(correctly specified), weighted Kaplan-Meier/Aalen-Johansen risks with death as a competing event.
The plan asks for agreement within the Monte Carlo SE of the truth. The gate, set before the first
run, makes this concrete for every risk, risk difference and log risk ratio at days 7, 14, 28 and 56:
|z| < 3, where z is the mean bias over its Monte Carlo standard error (combined with that of the
truth), a Bonferroni bound for 16 cells at a family-wise 5%. Bias over the empirical SE and the
coverage of the 95% confidence intervals are reported. The same analyses with the default
99th-percentile weight truncation are reported, not gated. Under process (a), when the analysis
uses the grace period of the process, the true risks of the binary-at-G regime and of the natural grace period are
identical by construction (`computeTrueRisks()` uses the same random numbers for both, and the effect
starts at the end of the grace period), so one truth serves both.

```{r gformula}
x <- tab("gformulaCells")
sameUnderTruncation <- isTRUE(all.equal(x$mean[x$gate == "reported"], x$mean[x$gate != "reported"]))
y <- if (sameUnderTruncation) x[x$gate != "reported", ] else x
y$bias <- formatC(y$bias, format = "e", digits = 1)
for (column in c("empSe", "modelSe")) y[[column]] <- formatC(y[[column]], format = "fg", digits = 2, flag = "#")
show(y, digits = 4, col.names = c("Weights", "Estimand", "Replicates", "Truth", "Mean", "Bias", "Empirical SE",
                                  "Mean model SE", "z", "Bias / empirical SE", "Coverage", "Gate"))
```

The bias criterion of the package's main simulation study, |bias| < 0.1 empirical SE, has a Monte
Carlo SE of about 1/sqrt(`r gformula$replicates`) = `r sprintf("%.3f", 1 / sqrt(gformula$replicates))`
here, so 0.1 is about `r sprintf("%.1f", 0.1 * sqrt(gformula$replicates))` Monte Carlo SEs. The largest
|bias| / empirical SE of the gated cells is
`r sprintf("%.3f", max(abs(x$biasOverEmpSe[x$gate != "reported"])))`
(`r sum(abs(x$biasOverEmpSe[x$gate != "reported"]) >= 0.1)` cells at or above 0.1), and the largest |z| is
`r sprintf("%.2f", max(abs(x$z[x$gate != "reported"])))`. With one binary confounder the weights take
few distinct values, and the 99th-percentile cap (taken over those values)
`r if (sameUnderTruncation) "leaves every estimate unchanged, so its rows are not shown" else "changes some estimates"`.

## ccwr on the lung cancer data

`ccwr` implements the clone-censor-weight analysis of Maringe et al. (2020) and ships its simulated
lung cancer data (200 patients; surgery within 182 days vs not). Two comparisons:

- **Outcome stage (gated).** Given `ccwr`'s clones and Cox censoring weights, our weighted
  Kaplan-Meier risks and Cox marginal structural model must equal `ccwr`'s, refitted with Breslow ties
  (`ccwr` uses Efron ties), to 1e-10 on risks and 1e-6 on the log hazard ratio and its robust SE.
- **Full pipeline (reported).** Each package builds its own clones and weights, with times rounded to
  whole days. Exact agreement is impossible: `ccwr` fits a Cox censoring model in the surgery arm where
  we fit the binary model at the end of the grace period, and its ties and same-day rules differ. The
  plan expects the 1-year risk difference and log hazard ratio within about one bootstrap SD, and
  bootstrap SDs within 10%.

```{r ccwrStage}
x <- tab("ccwrOutcomeStage")
x$difference <- formatC(x$difference, format = "e", digits = 1)
show(x, digits = 10, col.names = c("Quantity", "ccwr", "CloneCensorWeight", "Tolerance", "Difference", "Gate"))
```

```{r ccwrFull}
show(tab("ccwrFullPipeline"), digits = 4,
     col.names = c("Quantity", "ccwr", "ccwr bootstrap SD", "CloneCensorWeight", "CCW robust SE",
                   "CCW bootstrap SD", "Difference / CCW bootstrap SD", "Bootstrap SD ratio (CCW / ccwr)"))
```

The `ccwr` bootstrap SD of the log hazard ratio comes from `emul_estimate_bootstrap()`; that of the
risk difference from the same public `ccwr` steps run on person-level resamples, because
`emul_estimate_bootstrap()` returns only the hazard ratio.

## Synthea: acute myocardial infarction and metoprolol

On the synthetic Synthea database, persons with a first acute myocardial infarction either start
metoprolol within 7 days or do not (`initiateWithin(0, 7)` vs `notInitiateWithin(7)`), with all-cause
death within one year as the outcome. Synthea assigns treatment timing by rule, so its confounding is
artificial: this is a test of plumbing, not clinical evidence. Both packages analyse the same random
subsample of 5,000 persons. `ccwr` uses a fixed list of covariates (5-year age groups, sex, the
Charlson index, and antithrombotic, lipid-modifying and ACE-inhibitor use in the prior year) in Cox
censoring models for both arms, and does not truncate weights. CloneCensorWeight is shown with the same
covariates, no prior and no truncation, and with its defaults (all baseline covariates, L1 prior with
cross-validation, 99th-percentile truncation). The plan expects the same direction and
overlapping confidence intervals. Counts below 11 are shown as "<11".

```{r syntheaCounts}
show(tab("syntheaInitiation"), col.names = c("Persons", "Start on day 0", "Start on days 1-7",
                                              "No start by day 7", "Deaths within 365 days"))
```

```{r syntheaEstimates}
x <- tab("syntheaEstimates")
show(x, digits = 3, col.names = c("Fit", "Risk, start", "Risk, no start", "RD", "RD lower", "RD upper",
                                  "HR", "HR lower", "HR upper", "Largest weight", "Same direction as ccwr",
                                  "HR CI overlaps ccwr's"))
```

`ccwr`'s Kaplan-Meier fit has no person-clustered variance, so its risk difference has no confidence
interval. The covariates of this extraction include records on day 0, which can follow the treatment
decision when treatment starts on day 0, as it does for
`r syn <- tab("syntheaInitiation"); syn$startDay0` of the `r syn$persons` persons;
`fitCensoringModels()` warns about it in both CloneCensorWeight fits. The fixed list has four such
covariates (the Charlson index and the three drug groups), the default fit every covariate of the
extraction. The estimates of the default fit go in the
`r if (isTRUE(as.logical(x$sameDirectionAsCcwr[3]))) "same direction as" else "opposite direction to"`
those of `ccwr`. The `TrialEmulation` comparison of the plan (start on day 0 vs never) was skipped because the
package was not installed.

## Not run

- **Webster-Clark et al. (2025) tutorial.** The plan gates the clone counts, end reasons and person-time
  of the 0–30 and 0–90 day regimes against the tutorial's `01_cloning_and_censoring.R` on its
  SynPUF-derived `baseccwcohort.sas7bdat`, with `"deviationFirst"`. The tutorial's data and code were
  not available when these results were made, and `haven` was not installed.
- **The Maringe 2020 gist translation**, whose sanity targets are a 1-year survival difference of about
  0.12 and a hazard ratio of about 0.607: the gist was not available when these results were made.
- **`ccwbalance`** (the natural-grace truth) and **`TrialEmulation`**: not installed.


## How the results were made

The scripts that make these results (one per comparison, with a reviewed transcription of Program
17.3) are kept with the developers' validation materials, not in the package; so is the runner of
the cross-check suite. The source commits of the CloneCensorWeight and Cyclops builds that made each
result:

```{r provenance}
show(tab("provenance"), col.names = c("Comparison", "Date", "CloneCensorWeight commit", "Cyclops commit"))
```

## References

Hernán MA, Robins JM (2020). *Causal Inference: What If*. Boca Raton: Chapman & Hall/CRC.

Maringe C, Benitez Majano S, Exarchakou A, et al. (2020). Reflection on modern methods: trial
emulation in the presence of immortal-time bias. Assessing the benefit of major surgery for elderly
lung cancer patients using observational data. *International Journal of Epidemiology* 49(5):1719–1729.
